newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed - mogas up, naphtha down.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed - mogas up, naphtha down.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Tuesday; naphtha dipped, gasoline gained and fuel was steady in what many dealers saw as a slow market. Brent crude CFDs were off about one cent.
Brent CFDs for the balance of this week were pegged at -38 cents under July, one cent lower than yesterday, while next week was at -35 cents under July, again one cent lower.

Traders said June 9-13 was done at -33 cents against July and June 15-20 was concluded at -39 cents under August Brent. A Dated Brent cargo was also though to have found a buyer, but details were not confirmed.
Gas oil crack spreads were also unchanged with 4Q holding at $4.80 while Q198 was pegged at $4.70.

Naphtha swaps dipped $1 a tonne with June at $187 value and July down to around $188. Physical markets were very slow and fob material available in northwest Europe and the Balctic pressured prices lower.
Gasoline swaps managed to continue last week's move higher with June pegged around $209.50, up 50 cents, while July move $1.50 higher valued around $201.50.

Traders said stockpilling of material in anticipation of a hike in gasoline excise in the U.K. budget on July 2 was a signigicant factor in June's paper strength. Wet deals were heard at $211.50 fob Rotterdam and $208.50 fob ARA for second half material.
Heavy fuel swaps were a touch stronger, but only marginally with June at $84.50, from $84/84.25 on Monday. Physical barges were done at $84.50 and $85.00.
